element.name: Market Agility & Competitive Pressure
element.documentation: In an AI-driven landscape the "cost of delay" is existential. If the bank cannot deliver features as fast as a startup or a tech giant, it loses market share.

element.name: Regulatory Resiliency & Social License
element.documentation: For a major financial institution, non-compliance with APRA CPS 230/234 is a threat to the banking license. Manual compliance is too slow and error-prone for an AI-speed world.

element.name: Systemic Sustainability & Complexity Management
element.documentation: Unmanaged architectural drift creates hidden debt that makes systems fragile. Left unchecked, the system eventually becomes too complex to change at any speed.

element.name: Human-to-Machine Operational Scaling
element.documentation: Human architects are a finite bottleneck. As AI agents produce changes at machine speed, it is physically impossible to review it all with traditional methods.

element.name: Executive Leadership & Board
element.documentation: Accountable for the banking licence, market position and the enterprise risk appetite. Holds the agility and compliance drivers.

element.name: Prudential Regulator (APRA)
element.documentation: External stakeholder. Requires demonstrable, continuous compliance with CPS 230/234 and sound model risk management.

element.name: Enterprise Architecture Function
element.documentation: Owns architectural coherence and the target state; carries the sustainability and complexity-management concern.

element.name: Delivery Organisation
element.documentation: Human engineers and AI delivery agents producing change at machine speed; holds the operational-scaling concern.

element.name: Risk & Compliance Function
element.documentation: Second-line assurance. Needs provable, auditable control effectiveness rather than after-the-fact manual evidence.

element.name: Time-to-market is falling behind AI-native competitors, risking market share
element.documentation: AI-native challengers ship customer-facing features in days; our human-gated change process takes weeks. Every release cycle the gap persists is a release cycle of lost competitive ground and revenue at risk — a board-level concern, independent of the architectural cause.

element.name: Human review cannot keep pace with AI-speed delivery
element.documentation: Change volume from AI agents already exceeds what human architects and reviewers can inspect; the gap widens monthly.

element.name: Architectural drift is accumulating as unmanaged risk
element.documentation: As-built systems diverge from intent with no systematic detection; hidden architectural debt is compounding.

element.name: Manual compliance evidence is too slow and error-prone
element.documentation: Control mapping and evidence collection are manual, lag delivery by weeks, and cannot be trusted at AI-delivery cadence.

element.name: Frictionless Architecture & Governance at Machine Speed
element.documentation: Sustain architecturally-sound, provably-compliant change at the speed and volume of AI-driven delivery — without a human review bottleneck and without accumulating unmanaged architectural drift.

element.name: Drift Detected and Reconciled Continuously
element.documentation: The as-built estate is continuously reconciled against as-designed intent: every deviation surfaces as a classified drift event and is remediated before it can accumulate as unmanaged architectural risk.

element.name: Approved Change Reaches Production at AI Speed
element.documentation: The lead time from an approved change to its production release matches the cadence of AI-driven delivery — specifications are generated and designs reused, not hand-authored, so architecture no longer gates time to market.

element.name: Compliance Proven Before Release
element.documentation: Every change reaches production already mapped to its regulatory obligations and evaluated against machine-readable controls — compliance evidence is produced at the gate, not reconstructed after the fact.

element.name: Accountable, Auditable Automation
element.documentation: Agentic delivery runs at machine speed while every decision it cannot deterministically validate has a named human owner, and every action it takes is recorded as contemporaneous, examinable evidence.

element.name: Deterministic Human Accountability
element.documentation: AI is advisory; the specification is deterministic; a human holds sign-off.

element.name: Forensic Auditability
element.documentation: Ability to reconstruct not just what happened but why a decision was made.

element.name: Policy as Code
element.documentation: All governance rules, compliance mappings, and architectural guardrails are expressed as version-controlled, machine-executable policy, not prose documents.

element.name: No Retrospective Compliance (APRA CPS 230/234)
element.documentation: The platform must never let a change reach production on a promise to check compliance later — every change requires a resolved, evidenced obligation mapping before the deployment gate, and continuous as-built/as-designed evidence afterward. Retrospective flagging does not satisfy APRA's continuous-assurance expectation.

element.name: No Autonomous Self-Validation of Agentic Decisions
element.documentation: The platform must not allow an AI agent to validate or approve its own agentic decision-making. Wherever SR 11-7 / APRA model-risk obligations apply, validation must be independent of the agent that produced the change, and every validation outcome must be documented as evidence, not inferred after the fact.

element.name: Privacy Mapping Is Mandatory, Not an Out-of-Band Check
element.documentation: Any change touching personal information must be automatically mapped to its Australian Privacy Act (APP) obligations before the deployment gate, and the control catalog must carry APP requirements as machine-readable entries the mapping checks against — privacy may never be handled as a manual, out-of-band review step.

element.name: Governed State Confined to Approved Sovereignty Boundary
element.documentation: The knowledge graph, audit ledger and control catalog must be hosted, processed and reconciled only within approved, in-jurisdiction cloud environments. No platform component may source, replicate or reconcile governed system state through infrastructure outside that boundary.

element.name: Automated Specification Generation from Graph
element.documentation: For every approved change request, the system must automatically derive a complete, executable architectural specification from the knowledge graph — with zero manual authoring by an architect.

element.name: Automated Regulatory Obligation Mapping
element.documentation: Every technical change must be automatically mapped to its applicable APRA CPS 230/234 obligations before a deployment gate is passed. No change may proceed without a resolved compliance mapping.

element.name: Pre-Deployment Compliance Gate Enforcement
element.documentation: The supervisory control plane must intercept and evaluate all agent-generated changes against the executable specification before they reach any test or production environment. Non-compliant changes must be blocked, not flagged retrospectively.

element.name: Continuous As-Built vs. As-Designed Reconciliation
element.documentation: The system must continuously reconcile observed system state (telemetry, deployed artefacts) against the knowledge graph's as-designed intent and surface any deviation as a classified drift event.

element.name: Mandatory Human Sign-off for Non-Standard Changes
element.documentation: Any change that cannot be deterministically validated against the executable specification must be escalated to a named human architect for explicit approval. The system must prevent autonomous resolution of ambiguous compliance cases.

element.name: Maintained Machine-Readable Control Catalog
element.documentation: The platform must maintain the full set of applicable regulatory obligations, policies and standards as version-controlled, machine-readable control definitions (OSCAL Catalogs and Profiles), kept synchronised with upstream regulatory content sources.

element.name: Curated Reusable Architecture Library
element.documentation: The platform must maintain a curated library of technology-agnostic architecture patterns, implementation blueprints and composed solution designs — each mapped to its applicable controls and threat model — as the reuse basis for all new solution architecture and specification generation.

element.name: Authoritative Digital Twin of System State
element.documentation: The platform must maintain a live, queryable graph of enterprise technology state — an intent plane and an as-built digital twin plane — as the single authoritative source of architectural truth that every other capability reads from.

element.name: Immutable Forensic Audit Ledger
element.documentation: Every agent action, gate decision, specification evaluation and governed state transition must be recorded to an append-only, queryable ledger usable as contemporaneous evidence for regulatory examination.

element.name: Architecture Knowledge Management
element.documentation: Maintain a live, queryable graph of the enterprise technology landscape — its components, policies, relationships, and regulatory mappings, across an intent plane and an as-built twin plane — as the authoritative source of architectural truth.

element.name: Executable Specification Generation
element.documentation: Deterministically produce machine-consumable architectural specifications from the knowledge graph, which AI agents and CI/CD pipelines consume as guardrails rather than human-readable documents.

element.name: Agentic Development Supervision
element.documentation: Constrain, monitor, and intervene in the behaviour of autonomous development agents in real time, enforcing architectural and regulatory boundaries before code reaches any environment.

element.name: Forensic Audit Recording
element.documentation: Record every agent action, gate decision, and specification evaluation into an immutable, queryable ledger that serves as contemporaneous evidence for regulatory examination.

element.name: Architectural Drift Detection & Reconciliation
element.documentation: Continuously compare observed system telemetry against the as-designed knowledge graph and surface deviations — strategic, structural, or agentic — in real time.

element.name: Human Oversight & Approval
element.documentation: Identify, route, and manage human architect approval for changes that deviate from deterministic specifications or present ambiguous compliance scenarios, through a defined, auditable sign-off process that upholds deterministic human accountability.

element.name: Control & Obligation Management
element.documentation: Maintain the authoritative, version-controlled library of control and compliance content — external regulatory obligations and the organisation's own policies, standards and controls alike — as OSCAL Catalogs and Profiles kept synchronised with upstream regulatory sources, and map every governed change to its applicable obligations.

element.name: Reusable Architecture Curation
element.documentation: Curate technology-agnostic architecture patterns, implementation blueprints and composed solution designs — with control mappings and threat models — as the reusable basis for new solution architecture and specification generation, and model candidate and future-state architecture options for governance decisions.

element.name: Shift Governance Into the Pipeline
element.documentation: Replace document-and-meeting governance with machine-readable specifications, controls and enforcement gates that run inline with delivery.

element.name: Operate a Living Architecture Twin
element.documentation: Maintain an authoritative, continuously-reconciled model of intended and actual architecture as the single source both humans and agents work from.

element.name: Curate Reuse Before Build
element.documentation: Make curated patterns, blueprints and control mappings the default starting point for every change, rather than bespoke design.

element.name: Architecture Knowledge Graph
element.documentation: Intangible resource — the graph of intent, controls, patterns and as-built state.

element.name: AI Delivery Agents
element.documentation: Human-equivalent resource — the agentic crew that produces change at machine speed.

element.name: OSCAL Control Content
element.documentation: Intangible resource — the machine-readable regulatory and control corpus.

element.name: Enterprise Architecture Practice
element.documentation: Human resource — the architects who curate patterns and hold governance decisions.

element.name: Accumulated Evidence Record
element.documentation: Intangible resource — the growing, append-only body of recorded agent actions, gate decisions and sign-offs that regulatory examination draws on.

element.name: Governed Architecture Delivery
element.documentation: Architecture as executable intelligence, applied to delivery: the specification, the controls and the guardrails are machine-readable artefacts that AI agents and pipelines consume directly. End-to-end value stream that turns an approved change into a compliant, twin-reconciled production release: baseline, specify, build, prove, release, reconcile.

element.name: Establish Control & Reuse Baseline
element.documentation: Curated controls, obligations, patterns and blueprints are in place to build the change against.

element.name: Specify the Change
element.documentation: A deterministic, executable specification is derived from the knowledge graph for the approved change.

element.name: Build Under Supervision
element.documentation: Development agents produce code, tests and manifests within enforced architectural and regulatory boundaries.

element.name: Prove Compliance
element.documentation: The release candidate is evaluated against the specification and the expected controls; non-compliant changes are blocked, not flagged later.

element.name: Release & Attest
element.documentation: A compliant release is deployed, human sign-off is captured where required, and every decision is recorded to the forensic ledger.

element.name: Reconcile & Remediate
element.documentation: Observed state is continuously reconciled against intent and classified drift is routed to remediation.

element.name: Deterministic Spec Generation
element.documentation: Scripted, template-driven generation of executable architectural specifications from the knowledge graph. AI recommends scope; human holds sign-off. Output is the deterministic intent consumed by the agentic crew.

element.name: Agentic Development Execution
element.documentation: Supervised execution of AI-driven development within supervisory control plane constraints. Consumes the executable specification, regulation, policy, patterns, and controls from the knowledge graph to generate code, test suites, and deployment manifests.

element.name: Automated CICD Gate Execution
element.documentation: The CI/CD pipeline with the agentic control plane woven in. Evaluates every artefact against the executable specification and policy-as-code gates before a release is permitted. Blocks on violation; escalates exceptions for human review; logs all gate outcomes to the immutable ledger.

element.name: Production Release
element.documentation: Compliant, traceable-to-spec deployment to production, triggered only after all gates have cleared. Automatically auditable end-to-end.

element.name: Architecture Reconciliation
element.documentation: Continuous, automated reconciliation of the Current State Architecture against the Transition State Architecture in effect — what should be true by now — so gaps planned for later states are not flagged as drift. Records classified drift findings in the Architecture Conformance Register for human review.

element.name: Drift Review & Triage
element.documentation: Ongoing human review and triage of drift findings as they are surfaced by Architecture Reconciliation. An Enterprise Architect approves architectural drift. Each finding's triage outcome is recorded in the Architecture Conformance Register.

element.name: Target State Definition
element.documentation: The Enterprise Architect defines and maintains the strategic Target State Architecture — where the estate should be heading — and the Architecture Roadmap that sequences the transition to it, taking open regulatory remediation milestones from the OSCAL POA&M as input.

element.name: Solution Design Composition
element.documentation: The Solution Architect composes implementation blueprints into a solution-specific Solution Design. Realized at application layer by fn-solution-compose.

element.name: Agentic Delivery Execution
element.documentation: GH #25: the stable business capability of turning a deterministic architectural specification into supervised, agentic development output, independent of the specific spec-generation/build process steps.

element.name: Release Management
element.documentation: GH #25: the stable business capability of deploying a gated, compliant change to production once all controls have cleared. Distinct from bfn-release-enforcement, which gates the release rather than performing it.

element.name: Drift Management
element.documentation: GH #25: the stable business capability of continuously reconciling the current state architecture against the target state architecture and reviewing and triaging the resulting drift findings, keeping each finding's status in the Architecture Conformance Register.

element.name: Policy-to-OSCAL Conversion
element.documentation: GH #7: the stable business capability of turning authored policy and upstream regulatory standards into machine-readable OSCAL Catalogs, tailoring them into Profiles and resolving those into Resolved Catalogs, independent of the specific authoring/conversion process steps.

element.name: Pattern & Blueprint Traceability
element.documentation: GH #7: the stable business capability of mapping OSCAL Profile controls onto reusable architecture patterns and deriving technology-specific implementation blueprints with tracked control enablement.

element.name: Architecture Strategy
element.documentation: The stable business capability of defining and maintaining the strategic target state architecture the estate is reconciled against.

element.name: Solution Design
element.documentation: The stable business capability of composing reusable implementation blueprints into solution-specific designs.

element.name: Release Controls Enforcement
element.documentation: GH #7: the stable business capability of gating a release against its expected controls before it is permitted to ship.

element.name: Controls Effectiveness Assurance
element.documentation: GH #7: the stable business capability of continuously verifying that deployed controls remain effective in BAU.

element.name: Policy & Standards Authoring
element.documentation: The Compliance Officer / Auditor authors a verbatim custom policy or standard document (e.g. Word/PDF), informed by upstream regulatory standards, using tools outside the platform. Has no application-layer realization — the platform's involvement begins when fn-ai-markdown- conversion ingests the resulting document.

element.name: OSCAL Catalog Generation
element.documentation: Converts authored policy content and upstream regulatory standard text into OSCAL Catalogs. Profiles are not produced here — every Profile, including a published baseline such as NIST SP 800-53B, is tailored by a human in Control Baseline Tailoring. Realized at application layer by fn-ai-markdown-conversion (AI-assisted conversion into Trestle-editable Markdown) followed by fn-oscal-conversion's Trestle round-trip.

element.name: Control Baseline Tailoring
element.documentation: The Compliance Officer / Auditor tailors an OSCAL Profile from one or more OSCAL Catalogs — selecting the applicable controls and setting their parameters — to reflect the organisation's obligations, policies and risk appetite. Human judgement; no application-layer realization yet.

element.name: OSCAL Profile Resolution
element.documentation: Automatically resolves a tailored OSCAL Profile against its source Catalog(s) into a Resolved OSCAL Catalog. Realized at application layer by fn-oscal-profile-resolve.

element.name: Pattern Control Traceability Mapping
element.documentation: The Enterprise Architect maps generated OSCAL Profile controls onto architecture patterns to capture controls traceability. Realized at application layer by fn-pattern-authoring.

element.name: Blueprint Control Enablement Mapping
element.documentation: The Enterprise Architect derives technology-specific implementation blueprints from a technology-agnostic architecture pattern, capturing control enablement status and gaps against the OSCAL Profile. Realized at application layer by fn-blueprint-authoring.

element.name: Controls Effectiveness Monitoring
element.documentation: Platform Operations watches whether deployed controls remain effective in BAU, against the same SSP the release gate checked. Realized at application layer by fn-effectiveness-monitor.

element.name: Regulatory Standard
element.documentation: Verbatim upstream regulatory standard text consumed by the platform (e.g. NIST CSF, NIST SP 800-53) — published in prose form, not pre-converted to OSCAL.

element.name: Policy / Standard Document
element.documentation: Custom policy or standard authored by the Compliance Officer / Auditor.

element.name: OSCAL Catalog
element.documentation: Machine-readable control catalog.

element.name: OSCAL Profile
element.documentation: Tailored control selection / baseline.

element.name: Resolved OSCAL Catalog
element.documentation: The flattened set of controls a tailored Profile actually selects, produced by resolving the Profile against its source Catalog(s) — the operative control baseline for downstream use.

element.name: Architecture Pattern
element.documentation: Technology-agnostic, reusable design with mapped controls.

element.name: Implementation Blueprint
element.documentation: Technology-specific realisation of an architecture pattern, capturing control enablement status and gaps.

element.name: OSCAL Component Definition
element.documentation: Control implementation claims for a reusable blueprint.

element.name: Solution Component
element.documentation: A deployed instance of an Implementation Blueprint, specialized for one technology and bound into a specific Solution Design.

element.name: Solution Design
element.documentation: Solution-specific composition of Solution Components, unique to one system, closely related to its discovered configuration items.

element.name: OSCAL System Security Plan
element.documentation: Control implementation for the specific Solution Design it is derived from — reconciled against discovered configuration items via the existing state-discovery mechanism, not a separate one.

element.name: OSCAL Assessment Plan
element.documentation: Scope and method for assessing the SSP's declared control implementations ahead of a release — deterministically derived from the SSP/profile scope, not a hand-authored planning document. Imported by the resulting OSCAL Assessment Results (OSCAL requires every Assessment Results instance to reference the plan it assessed against).

element.name: OSCAL Assessment Results
element.documentation: Findings on whether the SSP's declared control implementations are satisfied. Verified at two cadences — a pre-release gate check and continuous BAU monitoring — each a specialised instance of this.

element.name: Release Gate Decision
element.documentation: Pass / block outcome with the controls evaluated at release time.

element.name: Control Effectiveness Evidence
element.documentation: BAU evidence that a deployed control is (or is not) working.

element.name: Current State Architecture
element.documentation: The discovered, as-built architecture of the estate — the "where we are" that is reconciled against the Transition State Architecture in effect.

element.name: Target State Architecture
element.documentation: The adopted, strategic future-state architecture — the "where we want to be" at the end of the Architecture Roadmap. Distinct from a Candidate Architecture Option, which is only under evaluation.

element.name: Architecture Roadmap
element.documentation: The time-sequenced transition from the Current State Architecture to the Target State Architecture — the Transition State Architectures in order, with the work that moves between them. Consumed by portfolio / delivery planning outside the platform; not read by any process in this model.

property.value: Plateau sequence with Work Packages and Implementation Events

element.name: Transition State Architecture
element.documentation: An intermediate, dated state on the Architecture Roadmap — what should be true by a given date. The one currently in effect is what the Current State Architecture is reconciled against, so gaps planned for later states are not flagged as drift.

element.name: OSCAL Plan of Action & Milestones
element.documentation: Open control deficiencies found by assessment — at the release gate and in BAU effectiveness monitoring — with their planned remediation and target milestones, in OSCAL form for external compliance reporting.

element.name: Drift Finding
element.documentation: A classified deviation of the Current State Architecture from the Transition State Architecture in effect — an unplanned gap.

element.name: Architecture Conformance Register
element.documentation: The system of record for every drift finding and its triage status — open, approved for remediation, accepted / waived, deferred to the roadmap, or closed. Findings approved for remediation are raised as work items in the ITSM backlog; the register itself is not a backlog.

element.name: Frictionless Architecture Platform
element.documentation: Governs architecture from authored policy through to BAU control effectiveness.

element.name: Controls & Compliance Catalog
element.documentation: Converts policy/standard documents (authored externally, outside the platform) into OSCAL Catalogs via AI-assisted Markdown conversion and a Trestle round-trip, and resolves tailored Profiles into Resolved Catalogs.

element.name: Reusable Architecture Library
element.documentation: Composable patterns, blueprints and solution designs with OSCAL references, threat modelling, and modelling of candidate / future-state options for governance to decide on.

element.name: Digital Twin & Knowledge Graph
element.documentation: Maintains the Architecture Knowledge Graph: an intent plane and a current-state digital twin plane.

element.name: Architecture Governance
element.documentation: Comparative evaluation of candidate options, impact assessment, the decision and its ADR, and archival of the rejected options with reasons. Pure decision-making — the options themselves are modelled in the Reusable Architecture Library.

element.name: Conformance & Drift Assurance
element.documentation: Supervises agentic development to enforce controls at build, supplies the expected controls the pipeline's release gate verifies, monitors effectiveness in BAU, and detects and reports architecture drift.

element.name: Modelling & Specification
element.documentation: Out-of-the-box ArchiMate / C4 / UML modelling, and generation of development specifications.

element.name: OSCAL Repository
element.documentation: OSCAL Catalogs, Profiles, Components, SSPs and Assessment Results.

element.name: Pattern & Blueprint Repository
element.documentation: Architecture patterns, implementation blueprints and solution designs.

element.name: Architecture Knowledge Graph
element.documentation: One graph store, two planes: Architecture Intent and Current-State Digital Twin.

element.name: Framework Pack Library
element.documentation: NIST / FedRAMP baselines; ArchiMate / C4 / UML metamodels.

element.name: Forensic Audit Ledger
element.documentation: Append-only, immutable record of agent actions, gate decisions, specification evaluations and governed state transitions, kept as contemporaneous evidence for regulatory examination.

element.name: Enterprise Architect
element.documentation: Owns principles, target patterns, options and governance decisions.

element.name: Solution Architect
element.documentation: Composes solution designs from implementation blueprints.

element.name: Security Architect / Threat Modeller
element.documentation: Runs threat models over patterns, blueprints and designs.

element.name: Developer
element.documentation: Consumes generated specifications for delivery.

element.name: Compliance Officer / Auditor
element.documentation: Authors control content and verifies traceability.

element.name: Platform Operations (BAU)
element.documentation: Watches control effectiveness and drift in run.

element.name: Source Control
element.documentation: Git repositories for specifications and delivery code.

element.name: CI/CD Pipeline
element.documentation: Builds, tests and releases; runs the controls enforcement gate inline.

element.name: Cloud & Infrastructure Platforms
element.documentation: Runtime platforms whose live state feeds the digital twin.

element.name: IT Service Management / Backlog
element.documentation: Delivery backlog and ticketing (e.g. Jira).

element.name: compliance-trestle
element.documentation: Third-party Python library/CLI dependency, not vendored source. Performs the Trestle Markdown <-> OSCAL round-trip behind fn-oscal-conversion.

element.name: LLM Provider
element.documentation: Language model used for drafting specs, ADRs, evaluations and threat narratives, and for converting verbatim policy/standard documents into Trestle-editable Markdown.

element.name: RFP / Vendor Submissions
element.documentation: Requests for proposal and competing vendor solution responses assessed at engagement time.

element.name: AI-Assisted Markdown Conversion
element.documentation: Use an LLM to convert a verbatim policy/standard document (custom-authored or upstream regulatory text) into the Trestle-editable Markdown catalog structure Trestle's author commands expect.

element.name: OSCAL Catalog Generation
element.documentation: Convert Trestle-editable Markdown into OSCAL Catalogs via a Trestle round-trip (import / author / assemble).

element.name: OSCAL Profile Resolution
element.documentation: Resolve an OSCAL Profile against its source Catalog(s) into a fully resolved OSCAL Catalog (trestle profile-resolve).

element.name: Pattern Authoring & Control Mapping
element.documentation: Author technology-agnostic architecture patterns and map them to OSCAL Profiles.

element.name: Blueprint Authoring & Component Mapping
element.documentation: Derive implementation blueprints from patterns and map them to OSCAL Component Definitions.

element.name: Solution Design Composition
element.documentation: Compose blueprints and patterns into a solution design and emit its OSCAL System Security Plan.

element.name: Threat Modelling
element.documentation: Attach threats and mitigations to patterns, blueprints and solution designs.

element.name: Future-State & Options Modelling
element.documentation: Model one or more candidate future-state architectures, including competing vendor / RFP responses, as decision input for Architecture Governance.

element.name: Digital Twin Ingestion
element.documentation: Build the current-state digital twin plane from live infrastructure state and deployment events.

element.name: Forensic Ledger Recording
element.documentation: Append every agent action, gate decision, specification evaluation and governed state transition to the append-only Forensic Audit Ledger as contemporaneous evidence for regulatory examination.

element.name: Comparative Evaluation & Decision
element.documentation: Compare candidate options, assess impact against intent and twin, record the ADR, and archive rejected options with rationale.

element.name: Agentic Build Supervision
element.documentation: Build-time control enforcement: intercept and evaluate every agent-generated change against the development specification and the expected controls before it is committed, blocking non-conformant changes. Every evaluation is recorded to the Forensic Audit Ledger rather than a separate evidence artefact.

element.name: Controls Enforcement Gate
element.documentation: Release-time control enforcement, run inline in the CI/CD pipeline: verify that every control the SSP expects is satisfied — directly on the release candidate for artefact-observable controls, and from the forensic ledger for process controls (e.g. no agent self-validation); block or pass.

element.name: Controls Effectiveness Monitoring
element.documentation: Monitor whether deployed controls remain effective in BAU and record the evidence.

element.name: Drift & Deviation Detection
element.documentation: Diff the current-state twin against the transition state in effect on the Architecture Roadmap and classify the deviations — unplanned gaps — as drift findings.

element.name: Modelling & Notation Rendering
element.documentation: Render ArchiMate / C4 / UML models against the bundled metamodels.

element.name: Specification Generation
element.documentation: Generate development specifications from patterns, blueprints and solution designs for spec-driven delivery.

element.name: Specification & Code Versioning
element.documentation: Commit and version generated development specifications alongside the delivery code that implements them.

element.name: Change Review (Pull Request)
element.documentation: Peer-review a proposed change against its specification and merge it, triggering a pipeline build.

element.name: Build & Test
element.documentation: Build and test a merged change and package it as a release candidate for the enforcement gate.

element.name: Release Deployment
element.documentation: Act on the gate decision — promote a passed release candidate to its target environment (or halt a blocked one) and record the deployment event.

element.name: Backlog Management
element.documentation: Prioritise and schedule remediation backlog items raised from classified drift findings through to closure.

element.name: Change Management
element.documentation: Maintain the change record for a release, attaching the gate decision as its compliance approval evidence.

element.name: Policy / Standard Document
element.documentation: Verbatim custom policy or standard document (e.g. Word/PDF), not yet machine-readable.

element.name: Regulatory Standard Document
element.documentation: Verbatim upstream regulatory standard text (e.g. NIST CSF, NIST SP 800-53), supplied as a document input -- not a system integration -- to fn-ai-markdown-conversion.

element.name: Trestle-Editable Markdown Catalog
element.documentation: AI-converted Markdown catalog structure ready for Trestle's author/assemble commands.

element.name: Regulatory Baseline Catalog
element.documentation: Upstream NIST/FedRAMP OSCAL catalog, e.g. NIST SP 800-53 rev5 via oscal-content -- used as golden-dataset validation data for the AI markdown converter, not a production pipeline input.

element.name: Regulatory Baseline Profile
element.documentation: Upstream NIST LOW/MODERATE/HIGH/PRIVACY baseline profiles (OSCAL Profile) vendored via oscal-content -- used as golden-dataset validation data for profile generation, not a production pipeline input.

element.name: Regulatory Resolved Baseline Catalog
element.documentation: Upstream FedRAMP LOW/MODERATE/HIGH resolved baseline catalogs vendored via fedramp-automation's bundled/catalogs -- used as golden-dataset validation data for profile resolution, not a production pipeline input.

element.name: OSCAL Catalog
element.documentation: Machine-readable control catalog.

element.name: OSCAL Profile
element.documentation: Tailored control selection / baseline.

element.name: Resolved OSCAL Catalog
element.documentation: Fully resolved/tailored control set produced by resolving an OSCAL Profile against its source Catalog(s) (trestle profile-resolve) -- the operative control baseline for downstream use.

element.name: OSCAL Component Definition
element.documentation: Control implementation claims for a reusable blueprint.

element.name: OSCAL System Security Plan
element.documentation: Control implementation for a specific solution design.

element.name: Architecture Pattern
element.documentation: Technology-agnostic, reusable design with mapped controls.

element.name: Implementation Blueprint
element.documentation: Technology-specific realisation of one or more patterns.

element.name: Solution Design
element.documentation: Composed solution — SolutionComponents under a SolutionDesign.

element.name: Threat Model
element.documentation: Threats and mitigations attached to a pattern, blueprint or design.

element.name: Live Infrastructure State
element.documentation: Observed configuration of the running platforms.

element.name: Deployment Event
element.documentation: A release / deployment recorded by the pipeline.

element.name: Current-State Digital Twin
element.documentation: The as-built plane of the Architecture Knowledge Graph.

element.name: Candidate Architecture Option
element.documentation: A proposed future-state or vendor solution under evaluation.

element.name: Target State Architecture
element.documentation: The adopted future-state architecture — the end state of the Architecture Roadmap.

element.name: Architecture Roadmap
element.documentation: The time-sequenced transition from current to target state — what should be true by when.

element.name: Architecture Decision Record
element.documentation: The chosen option with its rationale and trade-offs.

element.name: Impact Assessment
element.documentation: Effect of a candidate option on intent and current state.

element.name: Archived Rejected Option
element.documentation: A not-chosen option retained with the reasons it lost.

element.name: Release Candidate
element.documentation: A build submitted to the enforcement gate.

element.name: OSCAL Assessment Plan
element.documentation: Scope and method for a pre-release assessment run, generated ahead of the gate check and imported by its Assessment Results.

element.name: OSCAL Assessment Results
element.documentation: Findings on whether an SSP's declared control implementations are satisfied.

element.name: Gate Decision
element.documentation: Pass / block outcome with the controls evaluated — the pre-release instance of an OSCAL Assessment Results.

element.name: Control Effectiveness Evidence
element.documentation: BAU evidence that a control is (or is not) working — the continuous-monitoring instance of an OSCAL Assessment Results.

element.name: Classified Drift Finding
element.documentation: A deviation of current state from intent, classified and prioritised.

element.name: Remediation Backlog Item
element.documentation: A drift finding promoted to actionable delivery work.

element.name: OSCAL Plan of Action & Milestones
element.documentation: Open control deficiencies from OSCAL Assessment Results — release-gate and BAU — with their target remediation milestones, for external compliance reporting.

element.name: Development Specification
element.documentation: Executable spec derived from patterns, blueprints and designs.

element.name: Notation Metamodel
element.documentation: ArchiMate / C4 / UML metamodel used to constrain modelling.

element.name: Ledger Entry
element.documentation: A single immutable forensic record — actor, action, target artefact, timestamp, outcome.

element.name: IT4IT: Value Streams
element.documentation: The root wrapper composing all 7 IT4IT value streams.

element.name: IT4IT: Explore
element.documentation: The value stream "Explore" is performed on the Scope Agreements developed in the Evaluate value stream. It ensures that all planned and accepted Portfolio Backlog Items are further detailed, budgeted, and sourced for Digital Products. This value stream continuously explores new features and/or future directions of a Digital Product aligned with strategic direction and business needs. It ensures that the Product Design evolves to facilitate innovation and optimize business outcomes.

element.name: IT4IT: Evaluate
element.documentation: The value stream "Evaluate" contributes to the business strategy and portfolio planning activities. It provides a blueprint for optimizing products, services, and investment Portfolio Management. This value stream is focused on the continuous assessment and evaluation of the entire Digital Product Portfolio to optimize co-creation and alignment of business and technology Strategic Objectives.

element.name: IT4IT: Integrate
element.documentation: The value stream "Integrate" creates a new Product Release. It covers the planning, design, development (or configuration), and testing of a new Product Release (in non-production environments), and makes the Product Release available for deployment and release into production. A new Product Release can also be related to an emergency fix needed to resolve a production issue (such as resolving vulnerabilities and critical bugs).

element.name: IT4IT: Deploy
element.documentation: The value stream "Deploy" is installing a Product Release into production. It can also imply the removal, disposal, or updating of an existing installed Product Release, so it is made available or unavailable to the customer. Many possible strategies for deploying a Product Release can be scenarios within the Deploy value stream; for example, deployment to a targeted audience, or deployment using a dark launch in which functionality is not directly released to consumers. If the user requirements and/or the characteristics of the Digital Product demand that the installed Product Release is improved, released, and deployed frequently, a drive to automate these value streams can emerge. To comply with regulatory requirements, organizations can require approvals and an audit trail of all the Changes made in production environments. The Deploy value stream ensures that all changes are tracked and related to a specific Product Release.

element.name: IT4IT: Release
element.documentation: The value stream "Release" ensures that the Service Offers for ordering a new, a change in, or the decommissioning of an Actual Product Instance or its support to them are offered to consumers. The Release value stream maintains the Service Offer Catalog, the catalog views, and the Service Offer promotion and information of available Service Offers to the consumer base so that the individual consumer can find and order Digital Products, or support for them. Service Offers should be made available for viewing and requests for access over multiple channels. This value stream publishes the Service Offers based on various triggers and inputs, such as:

element.name: IT4IT: Operate
element.documentation: The value stream "Operate" monitors and ensures that the availability and performance of Actual Product Instances are within the boundaries of their agreed Service Contract and Key Performance Indicator (KPI) targets. The scope of this value stream includes managing any compliance and security aspects of running Digital Product Instances and underlying systems that may result from deployment and/or fulfillment. The IT4IT Standard describes how to achieve this using integrated, automated, or fully autonomous data flows between the event monitoring (Event, Incident, Change, Configuration, and Problem Management) functions of the digital services. In addition, the data flows may be designed to be reactive, proactive, or predictive, and include a retrospective.

element.name: IT4IT: Consume
element.documentation: The value stream "Consume" manages the lifecycle of consuming a Digital Product. Digital Products are consumed as services and the lifecycle is managed as a Subscription to the service.

element.name: Explore: Refine Product Backlog
element.documentation: The purpose of the value stream stage "Refine Product Backlog" is to translate a Scope Agreement into smaller pieces of work that can be assigned to product level features and linked to the product backlog. This includes organizing assigned backlog items into work packages and adjusting the Scope Agreement, business case, and budget as needed. The deliverables for this value stream stage are established Architecture Roadmap Items.

element.name: Explore: Prioritize Backlog Items
element.documentation: The purpose of the value stream stage "Prioritize Backlog Items" is to refine qualified Portfolio Backlog Items and mandates for new or existing Digital Product investment decisions. The budget allocated in the Evaluate value stream for the Product Portfolio is used to explore Digital Product ideas and determine feasibility. This should include ensuring that scoped Product Backlog Items deliver value, mitigate risks, and meet governance criteria (technology, security, reliability, supportability, etc.). The deliverables for this value stream stage are a Scope Agreement with prioritized Product Backlog Items; scope and timing refined.

element.name: Explore: Finalize Roadmap & Scope Agreement
element.documentation: The purpose of the value stream stage "Finalize Roadmap & Scope Agreement" is to assign work and begin to conduct planning meetings on a regular cadence. Stakeholder buy-in and agreement to the Release roadmap and outcomes must be obtained. This includes setting up tracking and reporting on progress. The deliverables for this value stream stage are an approved Architecture Roadmap and outcomes.

element.name: Evaluate: Gather Influencers
element.documentation: The purpose of the value stream stage "Gather Influencers" is to bring together inputs for a planning cycle. Typical inputs include: consumer demand, improvement ideas, new technology opportunities, technology lifecycle events (e.g., end-of-life), and any known policy (legal and regulatory demands) or budget constraints for the Digital Product Portfolio. Other inputs may include an internal and/or external environmental scan to identify strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats. Discussion with the business is centered on Digital Product value delivery for consumers and corresponding policy requirements. The deliverable for this value stream stage is new or updated Strategic Themes and/or Strategic Objectives.

element.name: Evaluate: Define Backlog Mandates
element.documentation: The purpose of the value stream stage "Define Backlog Mandates" is to determine if there are any mandates or directives that will impact the Product Portfolio, and to ensure mandates are clearly defined in backlog items and related in Scope Agreements. This should include a review of the existing portfolio and managed service provider agreements. Portfolio rationalization to balance the portfolio should be completed regularly and may generate backlog items that are bundled into Scope Agreements. Upon approval to proceed on a Scope Agreement, initial funding is allocated to the Explore value stream to identify concerns specific to a Digital Product and determine feasibility. The deliverables for this value stream stage are refined Scope Agreements to reflect mandates and defined Architecture Roadmap Items.

element.name: Evaluate: Propose Investments
element.documentation: The purpose of the value stream stage "Propose Investments" is to prioritize a list of opportunities and associated Scope Agreements. The prioritization should be based on a scoring method that considers business value, risk, costs, time, and resource availability. Scope Agreements are evaluated to determine if there is already a solution in the Product Portfolio that can be used or modified to satisfy the business need. If it is determined that there is not an existing solution and the new demand is in alignment with the digital strategy, the Scope Agreement is assessed against other work in the Portfolio Backlog and prioritized accordingly. The prioritization criteria should also consider factors like urgency and the impact of opportunities. The deliverable for this value stream stage is updated Scope Agreements with clarifications discovered during a prioritization of opportunities.

element.name: Integrate: Plan Product Release
element.documentation: The purpose of the value stream stage "Plan Product Release" is to plan all development and testing activities required for creating the Product Release. Multiple teams may be needed, and different development methodologies may be used. This value stream stage is revisited as it oversees the other value stream stages in this value stream to cater for changes in the planning and iterations of the Design & Develop value stream stage.

element.name: Integrate: Design & Develop
element.documentation: The purpose of the value stream stage "Design & Develop" is to analyze the requirements, create (or update) the design artifacts, and develop the changes (and associated Test Cases) for the Product Release. This includes the coding and configuration of software and related infrastructure (e.g., infrastructure as code).

element.name: Integrate: Accept & Publish Release
element.documentation: The purpose of the value stream stage "Accept and Publish Release" is to accept the Product Release as a candidate for deployment into production. The required change authority, such as the Product Manager, accepts the Product Release for deployment and/or release into production. The Product Manager accepts the Product Release after engaging with relevant stakeholders, which includes reviewing test results to accept or reject the list of remaining Defects, and reviewing the collateral produced. In a DevOps model, Operations has been participating all along but at this point an approval is given for the Product Release to be deployed into production.

element.name: Deploy: Plan & Approve Deployment
element.documentation: The purpose of the value stream stage "Plan & Approve Deployment" is to create a deployment plan for a Digital Product and, based on this plan, to sign it off with all relevant stakeholders.

element.name: Deploy: Fulfill Deployment
element.documentation: The purpose of the value stream stage "Fulfill Deployment" is to execute the Fulfillment Orchestration when the change window for deployment is open. The Fulfillment Orchestration is documented in the change records and can be coded as part of the Product Release to automate the Fulfillment Orchestration.

element.name: Deploy: Validate Deployment
element.documentation: The purpose of the value stream stage "Validate Deployment" is to ensure that all aspects of the deployment activities were correctly executed. This includes checking that the Product Instance is indeed running and configured according to plan, and that the monitoring and documentation associated is configured and made available.

element.name: Release: Define Service Offer
element.documentation: The purpose of the value stream stage "Define Service Offer" is to obtain the Service Offer information from the Integrate value stream and to plan the creation and publication of Service Offers to Consumers. Offers can also represent the consumption of cloud services making the Service catalog an Aggregation catalog between their own and cloud services; planning should take place to identify which cloud Service Offers would be made available.

element.name: Release: Implement Service Offer
element.documentation: The purpose of the value stream stage "Implement Service Offer" is to onboard the Service Offer into the Service Offer Catalog and to prepare all that is needed so that the Service Offer can be published.

element.name: Release: Publish Service Offer
element.documentation: The purpose of the value stream stage "Publish Service Offer" is to activate or release the Service Offer so that it can be ordered by consumers.

element.name: Operate: Detect Issue
element.documentation: The purpose of the value stream stage "Detect Issue" is to detect issues in an Actual Product Instance or system that has caused or may cause degradation of the service or breach the agreed service levels, then to prioritize and assign them for further diagnosis in a structured and repeatable manner.

element.name: Operate: Diagnose Issue
element.documentation: The purpose of the value stream stage "Diagnose Issue" is to prepare the best/quickest course of action to retain or restore normal operations. Further diagnosis can be performed to identify the root cause(s) of a potential or detected issue.

element.name: Operate: Resolve Issue
element.documentation: The purpose of the value stream stage "Resolve Issue" is to execute the (prepared) course of action to retain, restore, and confirm normal service operations.

element.name: Consume: Agree to Service Offer
element.documentation: The purpose of the value stream stage "Agree to Service Offer" is to get agreement from the customer to the terms and conditions of the Service Contract.

element.name: Consume: Subscribe to Service Offer
element.documentation: The purpose of the value stream stage "Subscribe to Service Offer" is to make the Actual Product Instance, as result of the Order and Desired Product Instance, available to the customer, in such a way that the customer is able to consume the Digital Product.

element.name: Consume: Select an Offer
element.documentation: The purpose of the value stream stage "Select an Offer" is to help the customer to select the Digital Product Service Offers(s) best suited to their needs.

element.name: IT4IT: Architecture Management
element.documentation: The ability to manage architecture is required to effectively describe the as-is and target architecture or 'blueprints' of the enterprise, to define the policies and standards used by it, and govern solution compliance to the defined architecture, policies, and standards. At an enterprise level, it includes enterprise architecture, the sub-domain specialties of enterprise architecture; at a tactical or service level, it includes solution architecture, service architecture, and systems (technology) architecture. The purpose of the Manage Architecture Capability is to use architecture policies and artifacts to provide the organization: - The ability to steer strategic decisions toward wanted positions and business outcomes (the future state) - The ability to proactively and holistically lead enterprise responses to business strategies and external drivers. - The ability to present business and IT leaders with recommendations to achieve target business outcomes and secure implementation of the transition roadmap.

element.name: IT4IT: Asset Management
element.documentation: The ability to track and report the value and ownership of capital assets throughout their life cycle.

element.name: IT4IT: Configuration Management
element.documentation: The ability to maintain information about Configuration Items required to deliver an IT Service, including their Relationships. This information is managed throughout the Lifecycle of the CI.

element.name: IT4IT: Defect Management
element.documentation: The ability to keep track of all Defects by registering Defects of all types (including security-related Defects). It analyzes Defects and finds resolutions. It also associates Defects with Requirements.

element.name: IT4IT: Demand Management
element.documentation: The ability to understand and influence Customer demand for Services and the provision of Capacity to meet these demands. At a Strategic level Demand Management can involve analysis of Patterns of Business Activity and User Profiles. At a tactical level it can involve use of Differential Charging to encourage Customers to use IT Services at less busy times.

element.name: IT4IT: Event Management
element.documentation: The capability to manage Events throughout their Lifecycle. Event Management is one of the main Activities of IT Operations.

element.name: IT4IT: Financial Management
element.documentation: The ability to manage an IT Service Provider’s financial accounts and to bill for and accept payment for services, or to make payment for services purchased and rendered. In an external provider archetype, may also include vetting of consumer credit applications and tax accounting.

element.name: IT4IT: Incident Management
element.documentation: The ability responsible for managing the Lifecycle of all Incidents. The primary Objective of Incident Management is to return the IT Service to Customers as quickly as possible.

element.name: IT4IT: Measurement & Reporting
element.documentation: Measurement & Reporting is the ability to consolidate information across the various value streams and functional components, to assess and evaluate metrics and KPIs, and provide service reporting, analytics, dashboards and scorecards.

element.name: IT4IT: Operations Management
element.documentation: The ability to perform activities carried out by IT Operations Control, including Console Management, Job Scheduling, Backup and Restore, and Print and Output Management. IT Operations is also used as a synonym for Service Operation

element.name: IT4IT: Policy Management
element.documentation: The ability to define and maintain the policies, principles, rules and standards governing the implementation to be compliant towards the target state.

element.name: IT4IT: Problem Management
element.documentation: The ability to manage the Lifecycle of all Problems. The primary objectives of Problem Management are to prevent Incidents from happening, and to minimize the Impact of Incidents that cannot be prevented.

element.name: IT4IT: Procurement Management
element.documentation: The ability to receive and execute purchase orders for supplies, equipment, products, and services, and to handle purchase exceptions.

element.name: IT4IT: Product Backlog Management
element.documentation: The ability to plan, resource, and execute a sequenced set of activities of prescribed duration that are managed together to achieve a defined scope of deliverables and other outcomes within established time, budget, and quality parameters.

element.name: IT4IT: Product Design Management
element.documentation: The ability to design new or changed service software functionality and data. Ability to identify the new or existing services required to meet the needs of the Scope Agreement and IT Initiative, including both service systems and service offers.

element.name: IT4IT: Product Development
element.documentation: The ability to implement new or changed software services application and data components by coding, code unit verification and defect correction.

element.name: IT4IT: Product Portfolio Management
element.documentation: The ability to create and manage the portfolio of services in plan, transition, production, and retirement with the aim to deliver the maximal aggregate value to the business objectives.

element.name: IT4IT: Release Management
element.documentation: The ability to plan, schedule and control the movement and installation of release configurations to test and live environments, while ensuring that the integrity of the environment is protected and that the correct components are released.

element.name: IT4IT: Request Management
element.documentation: The ability to provide a channel for users to request and receive offered services.

element.name: IT4IT: Requirements Management
element.documentation: The ability to manage requirements through the lifecycle of a service. It collects, refines, scopes, and tracks progress of and maintains requirements before and after an IT Initiative(s) ha(s)(ve) been delivered. It maintains the traceability of each requirement to the original source (demand, IT or business standard or policy, and/or requestor) and to the source (code), solutions and/or test cases throughout the service lifecycle. Requirements can be maintained for different levels. For example: - At an enterprise level, external market business and IT requirements are maintained; - At a tactical or service automation level, software process and service automation requirements are managed; - At an operational level, performance and availability requirements are managed.

element.name: IT4IT: Service Catalog Management
element.documentation: The ability to publish and maintain a database or structured Document with information about all Live IT Services, including those available for deployment. It also includes the set of services available for reuse in the development of applications and other services. The former are contracted for via SLA, the latter by OLA.

element.name: IT4IT: Service Level Management
element.documentation: The ability to define and negotiate service warranties and qualities of service that comprise standard or custom service level offerings, and to govern compliance to them. SLM is responsible for ensuring that all IT Service Management Processes, Operational Level Agreements, and Underpinning Contracts, are appropriate for the agreed Service Level Targets. SLM monitors and reports on Service Levels, and holds regular Customer reviews.

element.name: IT4IT: Test Management
element.documentation: The ability to plan and execute tests that ensure the IT service will support the customer’s requirements at the agreed service levels. It prepares test environment, plans and designs tests, and executes all functional and non-functional tests including performance and stress testing.

element.name: IT4IT: Vendor Management
element.documentation: The ability to ensure that all Contracts and agreements with Internal and External Service Providers/Suppliers support the needs of the Business, and that all Internal and External Service Providers/Suppliers meet their contractual/agreed commitments.

element.name: IT4IT: Availability Management
element.documentation: The ability to define, analyze, Plan, measure and improve all aspects of the Availability of IT Services. Availability Management is responsible for ensuring that all IT Infrastructure, Processes, Tools, Roles, etc. are appropriate for the agreed Service Level Targets for Availability.

element.name: IT4IT: Capacity Management
element.documentation: The ability to ensure that the Capacity of IT Services and the IT Infrastructure is able to deliver agreed Service Level Targets in a Cost Effective and timely manner. Capacity Management considers all Resources required to deliver the IT Service, and plans for short-, medium- and long-term Business Requirements. The Resources used by each IT Service and the pattern of usage over time are collected, recorded, and analyzed for use in the Capacity Plan.

element.name: IT4IT: Change Management
element.documentation: The ability to control the lifecycle of all changes from request to resolution. The primary objective of Change Management is to enable beneficial Changes to be made with minimum disruption to Services.

element.name: IT4IT: Collaboration
element.documentation: The Collaboration & Communication function supports many other IT4IT Functional Components by enabling optimal collaboration and communication between the various stakeholders and parties within the ecosystem, including internal and external collaboration with all parties in the digital ecosystem. Source: IT4IT 3.0.1 standard, section 10.6 (undocumented in the ArchiMate exchange file; pulled from the published standard PDF instead).

element.name: IT4IT: Compliance Management
element.documentation: Part of the combined IT4IT Governance, Risk, & Compliance function: ensures that security, risk, and compliance are fully embedded into the digital delivery network, including all involved parties and vendors, with transparency and traceability of compliance information — including continuous monitoring of compliance, audit management (performing audits to identify issues and exceptions), and managing deviations/exceptions. Source: IT4IT 3.0.1 standard, section 10.2 (the standard does not define Compliance Management separately from Risk Management — see it4it-cap-risk-mgmt; undocumented in the ArchiMate exchange file).

element.name: IT4IT: Continuity Management
element.documentation: The ability to manage improvements to IT Service Management Processes and IT Services. The Performance of the IT Service Provider is continually measured and improvements are made to Processes, IT Services and IT Infrastructure in order to increase Efficiency, Effectiveness, and Cost Effectiveness.

element.name: IT4IT: Contract Management
element.documentation: Manages the Contract — the relationship between provider and consumer created when an Offer is accepted and a Digital Product Instance is created — including all details required for financial recording, governance, measurement, charging, support, and servicing of that instance. Source: IT4IT 3.0.1 standard, sections 2.1 and 4.2.3. Caveat: the standard does not define a distinct "Contract Management" function or capability — this is adapted from its definitions of the Contract concept and the Contract Definition data object; contract management systems are explicitly called out as non-normative Supporting Capabilities supplied externally.

element.name: IT4IT: Customer Relationship Management
element.documentation: The ability to maintain relationships with service consumers. In an Internal IT Provider archetype, Business Relationship Management or BRM is the the capability to maintain a Relationship with the internal enterprise Line of Business Unit consumers and stakeholders. Business Relationship Management usually includes: - Managing personal Relationships with Business managers; Providing input to Service Portfolio Management - Ensuring that the IT Service Provider is satisfying the Business needs of the Customers. - In an External Service Provider context, Customer Relationship or CRM, which means it is the ability to do the BRM, except it is not with internal but with external customers and organizations.

element.name: IT4IT: Customer/User Support
element.documentation: The ability to assist users with interactions to service support. The support capability is be provided via varity of media (e.g. click, call, face), assists VIP's, allows for self-help, has the ability to list current disruptions and routes interactions to the correct supporting agents.

element.name: IT4IT: Deployment Management
element.documentation: Inferred, not sourced: the standard names no "Deployment Management" function or functional component anywhere — confirmed absent from both the ArchiMate exchange file and the full published IT4IT 3.0.1 standard PDF, and no definition could be found via web search either. This description is inferred from the Deploy value stream's stages (Plan & Approve, Fulfill, Observe, Validate): the ability to plan, execute, and validate the release of a Release Package into a target environment, and to observe and roll back that deployment if it fails validation. Treat this as a best-effort placeholder, not an authoritative IT4IT definition.

element.name: IT4IT: Identity and Access Management
element.documentation: The ability to design, develop manage, and control the security of automation services and information to meet requirements. The capability to ensure the Confidentiality, Integrity and Availability of an Organization’s Assets, information, data and IT Services. Authorization and Access Management usually forms part of an organizational approach to Security Management that has a wider scope than the IT Service Provider, and includes handling of paper, building access, phone calls, etc., for the entire organization.

element.name: IT4IT: Knowledge Management
element.documentation: The ability to gather, analyze, store and share knowledge and information within an Organization. The primary purpose of Knowledge Management is to improve Efficiency by reducing the need to rediscover knowledge.

element.name: IT4IT: Performance Management
element.documentation: The ability responsible for day-to-day Performance Management Activities. These include monitoring, threshold detection, Performance analysis and Tuning, and implementing changes related to Performance and Capacity.

element.name: IT4IT: Portfolio Backlog Management
element.documentation: The ability to provide lifecycle management and visibility of Portfolio Backlog Items as grouped into collections of work and prioritized; supports the Evaluate, Explore, and Integrate value streams. Source: IT4IT 3.0.1 standard, section 6.2.1 "Portfolio Backlog Functional Component" (undocumented in the ArchiMate exchange file; pulled from the published standard PDF instead).

element.name: IT4IT: Product Sales Management
element.documentation: The ability to generate, accept, approve, and manage customer orders for products and services.

element.name: IT4IT: Risk Management
element.documentation: Part of the combined IT4IT Governance, Risk, & Compliance function: the ability to identify, classify, manage, and mitigate risk in an increasingly complex digital environment, including maintaining a risk register, performing risk assessments (including vendor risk), and defining and implementing mitigation plans. Source: IT4IT 3.0.1 standard, section 10.2 (the standard does not define Risk Management separately from Compliance Management — see it4it-cap-compliance-mgmt; undocumented in the ArchiMate exchange file).

element.name: IT4IT: Strategy Management
element.documentation: The ability to create establish business strategies and business plans to increase customer value, to lead the direction for the organization into the future, to develop and harmonize the organizations strategic landscape and to develop competitive business strategies.

element.name: IT4IT: Workforce Management
element.documentation: Supports the HR Management aspects within the digital delivery model, ensuring the resource portfolio, skills, and competencies are aligned with the strategic direction — including onboarding/off-boarding, team administration, resource allocation, and employee career development. Source: IT4IT 3.0.1 standard, section 10.3 (undocumented in the ArchiMate exchange file; pulled from the published standard PDF instead).

element.name: IT4IT: Strategy to Portfolio
element.documentation: The value-stream domain covering the capabilities that shape enterprise and solution strategy into a governed portfolio of demand.

element.name: IT4IT: Requirement to Deploy
element.documentation: The value-stream domain covering the capabilities that take a requirement through design, development, and release readiness.

element.name: IT4IT: Request to Fulfill
element.documentation: The value-stream domain covering the capabilities that take a customer request through to a fulfilled, billed service.

element.name: IT4IT: Detect to Correct
element.documentation: The value-stream domain covering the capabilities that detect, diagnose, and resolve operational issues to assure service delivery.

element.name: IT4IT: Investigate a New Digital Product Idea
element.documentation: The trigger for this scenario is a Scope Agreement and an initial budget allocation to invest in a new Digital Product idea or enhancement that has a strong value proposition and alignment to one or more Strategic Objectives. The outcome is validation that the new product idea has a strong value proposition, alignment to one or more Strategic Themes, and will comply with technology standards and policy.

element.name: IT4IT: Retire Digital Product
element.documentation: The trigger for this scenario is a Scope Agreement and an initial budget allocation that incorporates Portfolio Backlog Items for retiring a Digital Product. The outcome is a decommissioned Digital Product, mitigating negative effects on consumers, impacts to dependencies, the re-allocation of resources, and the archival of data.

element.name: IT4IT: Digital Product Vision, Design, and Product Roadmap
IT4IT: Optimize a Digital Product
element.documentation: The trigger for this scenario is a Scope Agreement and an initial budget allocation that incorporates Portfolio Backlog Items for optimizing a Digital Product. The outcome is an enhanced Digital Product, based on innovating new features and addressing Defects, mandates, and technical debt.

element.name: IT4IT: Refine Digital Product Feasibility
element.documentation: The trigger for this scenario is a portfolio-level Scope Agreement with a decision to invest in a new or existing product. Product planning cycles further detail the budget, resource allocation, and feasibility for planned and accepted Portfolio Backlog Items. The outcome is a product-level Scope Agreement that further details the scope and budget for a Product Design and the optimization of business outcomes.

element.name: IT4IT: Rationalize the Product Portfolio
element.documentation: The trigger for this scenario is a business requirement to rationalize and balance the Digital Product Portfolio. The outcome is a Scope Agreement and resource allocation focused on Portfolio Backlog Items for the portfolio rationalization types: Retain, Replace, Re-Build, Retire — imperative to maintain a healthy and balanced portfolio by minimizing Digital Product technical debt and capability redundancy.

element.name: IT4IT: Plan Product Portfolio Investments
element.documentation: The trigger for this scenario is a portfolio planning increment (weekly, monthly, or annual). The Product Portfolio provides information about the health of existing Digital Products and new product strategy, supporting decisions for investing or reinvesting. The outcome is a Scope Agreement that provides the required scope and funding for portfolio-related concerns.

element.name: IT4IT: Perform Digital Product Governance
element.documentation: The trigger for this scenario is the Change Management of Digital Products. The outcome is a secure, quality, consumer-friendly, cost-effective Digital Product that aligns with Strategic Objectives, Architecture Principles, technology standards, and financial and policy constraints, ensuring traceability of the Digital Product lifecycle from Strategy to Development and into Operations.

element.name: IT4IT: Consider a New Digital Product
element.documentation: The trigger for this scenario is a business requirement for a new Digital Product. The outcome is a Scope Agreement and resource allocation focused on Portfolio Backlog Items and Strategic Objectives, indicating there is a strong business case for a new Digital Product.

element.name: IT4IT: Prioritized Digital Product Portfolio and Architecture Roadmap
IT4IT: Configure an Off-the-Shelf or SaaS Product for Use
element.documentation: Off-the-Shelf applications and SaaS solutions need to be integrated in a business Value Stream and supporting infrastructure environments, which might include the configuration of the application software. The Scope Agreement contains the mandate to contract the software or SaaS solution with the vendor and configure the product to fit the specific business Value Stream and supporting infrastructure.

element.name: IT4IT: Develop a New or Initial Product Release
element.documentation: A Product Release is developed — software and/or infrastructure — in-house or (partly) sourced with an external partner, using either a traditional waterfall or an iterative approach inside the Design & Develop value stream stage.

element.name: IT4IT: Update of a Vendor Product
IT4IT: Deliver an Emergency Change or Hotfix
element.documentation: The Integrate value stream can be triggered by the Operate value stream in case a Defect needs to be created. The Build Package of the Digital Product in Operations is changed to fix the Defect, after which a new Product Release is delivered; it is then investigated whether the fix also needs to be backported to the newest Product Release under development, to prevent regression issues.

element.name: IT4IT: Deploy a New Product Release Version for a Digital Product
element.documentation: Plan, prepare, and update the existing Actual Product Instances to ensure a stable Product Instance after the Deploy value stream is completed. The plan should include a "point of no return" in time and a rollback-to- last-known-good-configuration plan, both practiced during development of the Product Release.

element.name: IT4IT: Deploy a First Product Release for a New Digital Product
element.documentation: Plan, prepare, and execute the deployment of the initial version of the Digital Product. Since no customer is yet using the product, available time slots might include office hours; during execution the Service Contract is activated, requiring instrumentation of the data for the metrics that will measure the Key Performance Indicator (KPI) targets.

element.name: IT4IT: Disable or Remove Existing Product Release Instances of a Digital Product
element.documentation: Completely or partly disable or remove Actual Product Instances of a Digital Product. Removing a Digital Product might require changes to the Product Design, and customer data may have to be retained and made available for the customer to view for a while.

element.name: IT4IT: Terminate a Service Offer
element.documentation: Remove a Service Offer from the catalog and stop it from being ordered in the future — whether because the all-encompassing Digital Product is terminated, or as part of a normal release cycle when new versions of the Digital Product become available.

element.name: IT4IT: Bundle Existing Service Offers
element.documentation: Combine multiple existing Service Offers into a single Service Offer, so customers only need to order one Service Offer instead of several.

element.name: IT4IT: Release a New Service Offer
element.documentation: Provide consumers the possibility to request a new Actual Product Instance of a Digital Product, or a new form of support on an Actual Product Instance — linking the Service Offer to existing support/fulfillment plans and promoting its availability.

element.name: IT4IT: Change an Existing Service Offer
element.documentation: Maintain an up-to-date Service Offer for consumers — e.g. a change of charged service price, underlying terms and conditions, fulfillment or support plan, or access to the Service Offer.

element.name: IT4IT: Ensure Disaster Recovery Objectives
element.documentation: Ensure that capabilities listed in the business continuity/disaster recovery plan can work within the boundaries of the Service Contract, so recovery objectives (MAO, RTO, RPO) remain within the agreed Service Contract and BIA.

element.name: IT4IT: Remediate Consumer Front-End Issue
element.documentation: Triggered when an issue is raised by or through the service desk; the outcome is restored consumer experience, normal service operations, and service delivery within the boundaries of the Service Contract.

element.name: IT4IT: Actual Product operated according to or exceeding expectation
IT4IT: Remediate a major Event or Incident
element.documentation: Triggered by a major event (e.g. full system outage, significant application failure); its outcome is that the service is restored within the boundaries of the Service Contract, through correlation, diagnosis, and coordinated remediation across multiple teams.

element.name: IT4IT: Remediate an Identified Back-End Issue
element.documentation: Triggered by an issue (a breach and/or vulnerability) or a potential future issue in the back-end infrastructure, platforms, applications, or user transactions; the outcome is that the service remains operational without affecting consumer experience and within the boundaries of the Service Contract.

element.name: IT4IT: Order an Actual Product Instance Modification
element.documentation: Look for, select, and obtain a modification to an Actual Product Instance — e.g. changing a Subscription, an asset, or access to a business application, or a lifecycle action such as start/stop/scale.

element.name: IT4IT: Order a New Desired Product Instance
element.documentation: Look for, select, and obtain a new Actual Product Instance by ordering a new Desired Product Instance based on an available Service Offer.

element.name: IT4IT: Order an Actual Product Instance Support
element.documentation: Look for, select, and obtain support for a running Actual Product Instance — supporting omni-channel access and self-service concepts to limit the interaction flow to people and provide direct remediation.

element.name: IT4IT: Order an Actual Product Instance Termination
element.documentation: Terminate a running Actual Product Instance — e.g. end a Subscription, return or decommission an asset, or end access to an application.
